english: The number of solutions of the equation $\sqrt3\sin x+\cos x+\sin\dfrac{3x}{2}=3$ in the interval $[0,500\pi]$ is ______.
hindi: अन्तराल $[0,500\pi]$ में समीकरण $\sqrt3\sin x+\cos x+\sin\dfrac{3x}{2}=3$ के हलों की संख्या ______ है।
solution: $\sqrt3\sin x+\cos x=2\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\le2$ and $\sin\frac{3x}{2}\le1$, so the left side $\le3$
solution_full: Range of $a\sin x+b\cos x$: $\sqrt3\sin x+\cos x=2\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin x+\frac12\cos x\right)=2\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\in[-2,2]$.
Also $\sin\frac{3x}{2}\le1$. Hence the left side is at most $2+1=3$, and the equation holds exactly when both terms take their maximum values at the same $x$.
This equals $1$ exactly when $n$ is even, $n=2m$. So the solutions are $x=\frac{\pi}{3}+4m\pi$, $m\in\mathbb{Z}$.
Number of solutions $=125$. (Forgetting the parity condition gives $250$.)
originality_note: New: a sum of a sin x + b cos x (maximum 2) and sin(3x/2) (maximum 1) equal to 3; the maxima occur together only on every second member of the first family, because sin(3x/2) has period 4pi/3 (way 5). Closest known: sin x + cos x = 2-type 'no solution by range' items and sin^4 + cos^4 + 2 = 4 sin x cos y. Different because: both maxima are attained, but only on a sub-family fixed by parity, and the answer is a count.
